title: Grace-period request squash + telemetry bridge to stabilize hosted API 5xx during escalations
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Summary: After repeated customer escalations during tenant surge events we observed coordinated 5xx waves driven by aggressive client retries and small timing skews across upstream SDKs. The immediate mitigation (rate deadening + tenant quarantines) reduced impact but recurring incidents show we need a durable defense that reduces retry amplification while preserving correctness for idempotent and non-idempotent workloads.

Goal: Implement a short frontdoor "grace-period request squash" to deduplicate semantically identical requests that arrive within a configurable window (e.g., 200-500ms) and a "telemetry bridge" that correlates per-tenant repeat-request patterns with kvcache eviction/compaction and kernel hot-path saturation. This ticket covers the design, implementation, canary rollout, and monitoring for the feature.

Scope and constraints:
- Target: Hosted API frontdoor + edge proxy (fast path) for requests with identical fingerprint (method+model+input hash+idempotency token if present).
- Ensure no correctness regressions for requests that rely on side effects (we only squash when idempotency token present OR the endpoint is known-safe for dedupe e.g., text generation with deterministic inputs).
- Window configurable per-route and per-tenant (default 300ms).
- Telemetry bridge will emit aggregated signals to Console/observability: "dedupe-rate", "dedupe-latency-add", "pre-dedupe-5xx-rate", "post-dedupe-5xx-rate", and per-tenant kvcache churn correlation.

Design notes:
1) Fingerprinting: use an HMAC-based input hash with route/model/version salt to avoid cross-tenant collisions; include idempotency token if provided.
2) Local squash vs shared store: prefer in-process coalescing for single-instance fanout (low latency) backed by a small redis or shared in-memory LRU for cross-instance squashing in heavy-fanout scenarios. Start with in-process coalesce and a lightweight shared Redis/Tiered-Cache fallthrough only if canary shows cross-instance misses.
3) Observability: emit trace annotations for coalesced requests and a synthetic-sample to the request timeline to make postmortems simpler. Add ML-driven alert that triggers when dedupe rate > 5% and 5xx rate reduction < 10% (indicator of false-positive dedupes).
4) Fallback & safety: if a coalesced request fails, the dedupe controller will surface the original error to all waiters but not trigger additional upstream retries. Implement a short jittered retry only for known transient errors (upstream 502/503) under feature-flag controls.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (feature dev): unit + integration tests, synthetic load harness, conformance tests for idempotency semantics.
- Phase 1 (canary): enable for 1% of tenants in region us-east-1 for 48 hours. Monitor metrics: per-tenant 5xx rate, p50/p95 latency, dedupe hit ratio, kvcache eviction rate, error dispersion.
- Phase 2: widen to 10% tenants and selected high-retry tenants (with opt-in from Solutions/SE) for an additional 72 hours.
- Phase 3: global ramp to 100% with staged parameter adjustments (window size per route).

Runbook & support:
- If post-dedupe 5xx rate increases, rollback via kill-switch at edge OR disable for offending tenant(s).
- Pager flows: the SRE oncall will be paged if cluster-level 5xx spike > 2x baseline or dedupe-induced latency regressions > 20% p95.

Success criteria:
- Reduce tenant-amplified 5xx incident recurrence by > 60% for canary tenants.
- No regression in correctness for non-idempotent routes (0 reported customer correctness bugs in first 30 days).
- Observability signals in Console for every dedupe event and a new "dedupe-action" audit trail for private deployment customers (compliance requirement).

Open design trade-offs:
- Aggressive dedupe windows risk masking legitimate concurrent requests (affects throughput/latency). We will mitigate by route-specific policies and conservative default window.
- Cross-instance dedupe requires a shared store which complicates operations; prefer in-process first to minimize blast radius.

Deliverables:
- RFC doc on Confluence: link below.
- Implementation PRs: edge-proxy and runtime adapters with feature flag gating.
- Tests: unit, integration, and chaos tests simulating SDK retry storms.
- Dashboards & alerts: new Console panels and SLO-adjusted alerts.
- Postmortem template additions for dedupe-related incidents.
comments: 2026-03-09 - Triage: incident triage summary appended; assigned to Diego Morales for rapid prototyping. Key ask from CS: reduce customer-visible 5xx within 24-48h and provide customer-level mitigation knobs.

2026-03-10 - Design review: Engineering + SRE reviewed the proposal. Agreed to conservative default window (300ms), limit initial scope to generation endpoints and to require idempotency token OR explicit route allowlist. Action: Confluence RFC created (see links).

2026-03-11 - Implementation note: PoC of in-process coalescer completed. Observed median added latency 6ms for coalesced waits, dedupe hit-ratio 12% under synthetic retry waveform. Starting PR for edge-proxy changes. GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/12345
2026-03-11 - QA: Integration harness found an edge-case where multipart streaming responses could deadlock when coalesced; added a bypass for streaming endpoints pending further work.

2026-03-12 - Canary kickoff: Enabled feature-flag for 1% tenants in us-east-1. Live dashboard created and smoke alerts configured. Initial 4h snapshot: 5xx decreased 48% for canary cohort, dedupe hit ratio 9%. No correctness reports yet.
2026-03-12 - Support coordination: Solutions Eng notified customers in cohort and added temporary support doc describing \"dedupe behavior\" and how to opt-out via header. Doc link in links field.
